qa.name: Deltoid — Anterior Head
qa.function: Flexion and medial rotation of the arm
qa.blood_supply: Anterior circumflex humeral artery, Thoracoacromial artery
qa.clinical_note: All three heads of the deltoid are tested together by resisted abduction — axillary nerve injury causes flattening of the shoulder contour

qa.name: Deltoid — Middle Head
qa.function: Abduction of the arm (from 15 to 90 degrees)
qa.blood_supply: Anterior and posterior circumflex humeral arteries
qa.clinical_note: Primary abductor of the arm from 15 to 90 degrees — works with supraspinatus which initiates the first 15 degrees

qa.name: Deltoid — Posterior Head
qa.function: Extension and lateral rotation of the arm
qa.clinical_note: Axillary nerve injury also affects teres minor — both are tested by resisted lateral rotation with arm at side

qa.name: Teres Major
qa.origin: Inferior angle and lower lateral border of the scapula
qa.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular groove of the humerus
qa.function: Medial rotation, adduction, and extension of the arm
qa.blood_supply: Subscapular artery, Posterior circumflex humeral artery
qa.clinical_note: Often called the little helper of latissimus dorsi — same actions, same insertion area; not part of the rotator cuff

qa.name: Coracobrachialis
qa.insertion: Middle third of the medial surface of the humerus
qa.function: Flexion and adduction of the arm at the glenohumeral joint
qa.clinical_note: The musculocutaneous nerve pierces coracobrachialis — entrapment here causes weakness of elbow flexion and loss of lateral forearm sensation

qa.name: Subclavius
qa.origin: Junction of the first rib and its costal cartilage
qa.insertion: Inferior surface of the middle third of the clavicle
qa.function: Depresses and stabilizes the clavicle; protects the subclavian vessels in clavicle fractures
qa.blood_supply: Clavicular branch of the thoracoacromial artery
qa.clinical_note: Acts as a buffer protecting the subclavian vein and brachial plexus during clavicle fractures — its own nerve is used to assess C5 and C6 root integrity
